unit.title: Unit 5: How to ask questions using 'Ba' and the 'Na' linker

content.text: In this lesson, you will learn how to ask questions in Tagalog and use the linker na.

list.item: Nag-aaral ba si Anna sa University of California?: Is Anna studying at the University of California?

content.text: In Tagalog, the word 'ba' is placed after the verb or subject to form a yes/no question. This structure helps to indicate that the sentence is a question rather than a statement. You can follow these patterns:
1. When the sentence starts with the verb:
Example: Nag-aaral ba si Anna sa University of California? (Is Anna studying at the University of California?)
2. When the sentence starts with the subject:
Example: Si Anna ba ay nag-aaral sa University of California? (Is Anna studying at the University of California?)

list.item: Nagtatrabaho ba siya sa ospital?: Is she working at the hospital?
Pupunta ba tayo sa park?: Are we going to the park?

content.text: 'NA' and '-NG' are used to connect adjectives and nouns:

list.item: The linker 'NA' is used to connect adjectives to nouns when the adjective ends in a consonant.
The linker '-NG' is used when the adjective ends in a vowel.
Mahal na asul na bag: The blue bag is expensive

question.text: How do you turn the sentence 'Nag-aaral si Anna sa University of California' into a question?

answers.answer: Nag-aaral ba si Anna sa University of California?
Si Anna ba ay nag-aaral sa University of California?
Nag-aaral si Anna sa University of California ba?
